comments:
Fragmentary manuscript of the Tibetan translation of Dharmottara's commentary on the Nyāyabindu (ID:5589) found in Tabo. 
Called manuscript "A" in Lasic's description ([N9KW4E38]: 64-65). (For manuscript "B", see (ID:8220).)
Lasic ([N9KW4E38]: 67pp.) argues that it represents the translation by Dharmāloka (ID:8394) and Jñānagarbha around 800, before it was revised by rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786).
name: rigs pa'i thigs pa'i rgya cher 'grel ba
item_description:
See [N9KW4E38]: 64-65.
Script: handwritten dbu can
Available folios: 3, 5, 9.
Average of 60 syllables per line.
7 lines per folio.
Orthographic peculiarities:
- inverted i
- combinations st and sp written vertically
- mi and me palatalized
- use of da drag
- particles following don have the form they would have after da drag: don tu, don kyi, don ces, don to
- indiscriminate use of ci ltar and ji ltar
